context:
One-line guard per loop -- require a non-empty derived path before the existence check:

    if [ -n "$bundle" ] && git cat-file -e "HEAD:${bundle}" 2>/dev/null && ...

Apply to all three loops (manifest, applied, plans/tuning). Do not change the --diff-filter=ACMRD choice: including deletions is deliberate and documented in the surrounding comments, and a removed companion beside a surviving bundle must still trip validation.

Add a workflow unit test alongside the existing tests/unit/workflows/test_validate_submission_changed_bundles.py that pins the empty-derivation case: a diff deleting a bundle+manifest pair must contribute nothing to CHANGED.

This must land as its own develop PR. The workflow's own self-green guard rejects any submission PR that touches validator or workflow files, so it cannot ride along with a corpus change.
description:
CONFIRMED by local reproduction on 2026-08-28 while opening PR #1940 (pre-2026-08-23 corpus withdrawal against published-results).

In .github/workflows/validate-submission.yml, the "Find changed bundles" step derives a paired primary bundle for each changed companion. It uses --diff-filter=ACMRD, so deletions are included by design (a removed manifest beside a surviving bundle must still trip validation).

When BOTH the manifest and its bundle are deleted, the awk lookup finds nothing and $bundle is the empty string. The guard is:

    if git cat-file -e "HEAD:${bundle}" 2>/dev/null && ! printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED" | grep -qxF "$bundle"; then

`git cat-file -e "HEAD:"` resolves to the ROOT TREE and SUCCEEDS, so an empty string is appended to CHANGED once per deleted manifest. Those empty lines reach /tmp/changed_bundles.txt and are passed as empty ARGV entries by `xargs -d '\n'`. scripts/validate_submission.py expands each empty path argument to the entire live bundles directory.

Reproduced directly:

    python scripts/validate_submission.py --require-manifest <one-real-bundle> "" ""
    -> Validated 19 bundle(s)      # 1 + 9 + 9, the live corpus twice

On PR #1940 (117 deleted manifests, 1 added bundle) CI reported "Validated 10 bundle(s): 11 error(s)" and failed every surviving bundle with "Submission manifest not found", plus one spurious "summary.validation must be 'passed', got 'partial'". None of those bundles were touched by the PR.

Fails closed (over-validates, red) rather than open, so it is a false-positive generator that blocks legitimate maintainer PRs, not a bypass.

Why it was not seen before: a PURE deletion PR leaves CHANGED empty of ACMR primaries, has_bundles=false, and the validate step is skipped entirely -- the empty strings are injected but never consumed. That is why PR #1882 (154-file withdrawal) passed. Only a PR that both deletes pairs AND adds/modifies a primary trips it.

All three companion loops share the defect: manifest, applied-ledger, and plans/tuning.

preserves.behavior: --diff-filter=ACMRD in all three companion loops: including deletions is deliberate, so a removed companion beside a surviving bundle still trips validation
The four-signal manifest waiver confined to auto/results-mirror-* bot PRs
set -euo pipefail in the Validate bundles step: it is load-bearing for the exit code through the tee pipe (see PR #1629)
